schema.description: One visit to give blood, as the donor service reported it. Written by hand readings of a note compiled from the service's emails; booked visits not yet held are not recorded. Version 2 adds source_time and requires it, every other rule unchanged.

centre.description: The donor centre's name as the service gave it.

date.description: The appointment's date and time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in Sydney local time. This is the fact time.

id.description: Identity, chosen by the reader: the service's prefix and the date.

note.description: Anything else the reader took from the emails about this visit.

outcome.description: What came of the visit, lower case: a word from the source's account of it (such as donated or attended), with a reader's gloss after a semicolon where the source leaves the result open.

product.description: What was given, as the service's emails name it, lower case.

source_time.description: How the visit's clock was read: value is date as the records file wrote it, read in zone. The records files state Australia/Sydney, the zone this Definition reads date in, with basis source. Required.

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.
